name: Web Workers
plain: Runs scripts on background threads with no prompt.
meaning: A site can use multiple CPU cores while the tab is open. Workers cannot touch the DOM but can run timers, network and compute, which is how miners and heavy trackers hide from the UI thread.

access.persistence: Dedicated workers end with the page; shared workers end when the last client closes
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Same-origin script only; module workers supported; blob: workers allowed

limits.headline: Can run extra code in the background while the page is open
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads or starts a heavy job.
can: Run heavy work on a second thread so the page stays smooth
Keep a worker running while the tab is open
cannot: Change what is on the page directly
Keep running after you close the tab
Use unlimited power; browsers slow hidden tabs
Reach other sites' workers or data

story.what_it_is: A page can run extra background workers, with no prompt.

marketing.name: Web Workers API
marketing.pitch: MDN says workers let a page run scripts in background threads so the main page stays responsive.

story.for_you: You never see them. Heavy tasks like photo editing run in the background so the page does not freeze while you type.
story.for_makers: Makers use them to keep pages smooth while crunching data. Bad actors use the same trick to mine crypto in your tab without telling you.

use_cases.example: A photo editor applies filters in a worker so sliders stay smooth.
A browser game runs physics and AI on a worker so the frame rate does not drop.
A video call tool blurs your background in a worker.
A hidden crypto miner runs in a worker in a shady site tab.
A web spreadsheet recalculates in a worker so typing stays quick.
Analytics tools process events in a worker to avoid slowing the page.

technical_bounds: Firefox limits to 512 workers per domain (dom.workers.maxPerDomain); Chrome has no fixed cap but memory limited
Background tabs throttle timers in workers just like pages; intensive throttling applies
SharedWorker returned to Android Chrome at version 148 (BCD); long absent on mobile
No access to window, document or localStorage; IndexedDB, fetch, WebSockets work
Worker script must be same origin (or data via importScripts with CORS)
